assumptions: Airless apparent body-centre positions; angular diameter is the equatorial full-disc width.
Input latitude is planetocentric; radial elevation uses a 1737400 m sphere in MOON_ME_DE421.
Horizons documents lunar mean-Earth orientation relative to DE421; actual source headers are retained.
Terrain visibility, illumination fraction and site safety have not been calculated.
Future UTC uses Horizons' current leap-second assumptions; cached acquisitions are not automatically refreshed.
Representative native DEM pixel in the named NASA study area; not a landing-site approval.
Selected nearest the tile centre with positive native LOLA sample count and finite quality layers.
Pixel-centre coordinates use the source CRS and NASA documented MOON_ME_DE421 frame.
DEM interpolation and uncertainty remain; local slope is not a lander-specific safety certification.
Bounds conservatively enclose the source tile; horizon visibility has not been computed.
DEMs use the NASA-documented lunar mean-Earth frame, metres and a 1737400 m sphere.
Sample preferred local terrain first, falling back only to valid source heights in the broader DEM.
Terrain sampling is bilinear; the finite radial/azimuth grid can miss subgrid or more distant obstructions.
Any unresolved sample makes the entire sampled ray unknown; no edge clipping or median-filled nodata.
Search radius 150000 m; azimuth spacing 0.25 deg; near/far radial spacing 5/20 m.
Complete coverage describes the configured sampled rays, not all possible terrain directions or distances.

Horizon method and parameters: true-bearing-spherical-raster-horizon-v1 {"azimuth_step_deg": 0.25, "coverage_definition": "All sampled points known within the finite search radius; angular/radial resolution limits remain.", "interpolation": "bilinear terrain, circular-linear skyline", "max_radius_m": 150000, "near_radius_m": 2000, "near_step_m": 5, "radial_samples": 7800, "radial_step_m": 20}
Horizon angles are circularly interpolated between supplied azimuths; missing endpoints remain unknown.
Sunlight hours are full-sun-equivalent hours from a uniform circular disc above a locally straight horizon.
Sun visible means any positive disc fraction; Earth visible means its apparent centre is strictly above terrain.
Each sample governs [MET_i,MET_i+1); the endpoint adds no duration. Event times are sample-limited, not refined.
Unknown positive-duration intervals make affected whole-mission metrics null; no missing time is silently counted.
Both-visible hours use any sunlight plus Earth-centre visibility; DTE is geometry, not guaranteed radio service.
Slope bands are project screening heuristics, not a lander-specific touchdown certification.
